title: LLM-MARK: A Computing Framework on Efficient Watermarking of Large Language Models for Authentic Use of Generative AI at Local Devices
problem: Watermarking schemes for LLM intellectual property protection have prohibitively high computation costs for real-time execution on local devices. Generative AI faces authentication challenges from data misconduct including counterfeit content and unauthorized model usage.
motivation: Efficient LLM watermarking at the edge is essential for IP protection and model authentication in the era of generative AI deployment.
method: The framework uses two hardware techniques optimized for speed: specialized hardware hashing (computing fingerprints directly in silicon for rapid lookups) and a pruned bitonic sorting network (a circuit that sorts data by removing unnecessary comparisons). These techniques are implemented on a Xilinx XCZU15EG FPGA—a programmable chip—to enable fast watermark verification even on devices with limited computing power.
key_novelty: The core contribution is combining hardware hashing and pruned bitonic sorting network acceleration to enable efficient watermark verification on resource-constrained edge FPGAs.
contributions: Hardware-efficient watermarking computing framework enabling LLM authentication on local devices
Specialized hardware hashing mechanism for fast watermark lookup
Pruned bitonic sorting network acceleration architecture
30x speedup demonstration on FPGA for practical edge deployment
limitations: Scalability to larger models and practical deployment on actual mobile devices not discussed.
primary_theme: Hardware-accelerated LLM watermarking for edge authentication
